newsitem.title: FINLAND: POSTIPANKKI SLIGHTLY UPS 1997 GDP GROWTH FORECAST.
newsitem.headline: POSTIPANKKI SLIGHTLY UPS 1997 GDP GROWTH FORECAST.

text.p: Finnish gross domestic product will increase 2.3 percent this year and 3.2 percent in 1997, Postipankki's economic research department said in a new forecast released on Thursday.

This year's GDP growth rate was unchanged from the bank's previous forecast in August, while he 1997 figure was now 0.2 percentage points higher, but still below the finance ministry's top-of-the-range 3.9 percent GDP growth forecast for 1997.
Postipankki saw Finnish consumer price inflation accelerating to 1.6 percent year-on-year in 1997 from 0.7 percent this year.
Its current account surplus forecast was for a rise in 1997 to 27.2 billion markka from 21.8 billion this year.

Postipankki said it was more pessimistic on investment than many other economic research institutes and financial market economists. It projected investment growth at 2.1 percent in 1997, down from 2.6 percent this year.

Contrary to recent opinions by senior finance ministry officials, Postipankki expected Finland's gross public debt to GDP to remain narrowly outside the 60 percent limit for Economic and Monetary Union. PSP's EMU debt figure was 61.4 percent this year and 60.6 percent in 1997.
